Question_text: GOP is an oil producer based in country X. It is a public corporation. GOP plans to build a 200km pipeline across the country using retained profits to pay for it. The pipeline will need planning permission from the Government. Environmental pressure groups are concerned. A spokesperson for GOP said: 'GOP's objectives are different to businesses in the private sector. This pipeline will create 2000 skilled construction jobs and reduce the need for other businesses to import oil.'
Sub_topic: Differences: private vs public sector objectives
Ethical issues: profit vs ethics conflicts

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'public corporation'?
Identify two economic objectives of country X's government.
Identify and explain two ways a pressure group might try to influence the actions of GOP.
Identify and explain two ways in which the objectives of GOP might be different if it was in the private sector.
Do you think the Government should allow GOP to build the pipeline? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Samira owns a successful business selling takeaway fried food. She employs 2 part-time workers. Last year revenue fell for the first time in 10 years. This was because of increased competition from a well-known franchise. To respond to this, Samira could lower her prices, as shown in Table 1. Another option is to start a delivery service. Samira plans to do some market research. She has to decide whether to use secondary research or set up a focus group with some of her customers. Table 1: Price and variable cost information for Samira's business Current price | New price Average price per item | $4 | $3 Average variable cost per item | $2 | $2 Forecast average number of customers per week | 200 | 300
image: A table titled 'Table 1: Price and variable cost information for Samira's business'. It presents a comparison between 'Current price' and 'New price' scenarios. The rows detail 'Average price per item' ($4 for current, $3 for new), 'Average variable cost per item' ($2 for both), and 'Forecast average number of customers per week' (200 for current, 300 for new).
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Pricing methods: cost plus, competitive, penetration, skimming, promotional
Primary methods: postal questionnaire, online survey, interviews, focus groups
Features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, profit, retained profit
Advantages, disadvantages of channels: wholesalers, retailers, direct

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'franchise'?
Calculate Samira's forecast weekly revenue if she lowered the price of her products.
Identify and explain two reasons why revenue is important for Samira's business.
Identify and explain two factors Samira should consider before starting a delivery service.
Do you think Samira should use secondary research or a focus group to gather market research information? Justify your answer.

Question_text: LBM is an online fashion clothing retailer. LBM's target market is 18-35 year olds. Last year revenue increased by 25% to $600m. The Marketing Director said: 'All businesses have to satisfy customer needs. Customer service is important which is why all employees receive induction training. LBM offers customers a wider range of products than its competitors. Promotion is through social media networks. Is there any reason to open our own shops?' LBM plans to add 3500 new styles each week and will need to arrange finance for the additional inventory.
Topic: 2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees
Sub_topic: Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Use of internet, social media for promotion
Advantages, disadvantages of channels: wholesalers, retailers, direct
Reasons for finance: start-up, expansion, working capital
Factors in choice: size, legal form, amount, time, loans

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'induction training'?
Identify two reasons why it is important for LBM to satisfy customer needs.
Identify and explain two problems for LBM of having a wide range of products available to customers.
Identify and explain one advantage and one disadvantage to LBM of opening its own shops.
Explain two suitable sources of finance that LBM could use to purchase additional inventory. Recommend which source of finance LBM should use. Justify your answer.

Question_text: NBV is a multinational company. It makes building products such as bricks. Last year NBV's financial accounts showed capital employed as $144 billion. NBV has operations in 18 countries and a total workforce of 400000. NBV experiences some diseconomies of scale. All raw materials are purchased from the countries it operates in to avoid problems with exchange rates. NBV plans to open a factory in Country B for the first time. Some people think this decision will only bring drawbacks for other businesses in country B.
Unit: UNIT 6: External influences on business activity
Sub_topic: Impact on importers, exporters: prices, competitiveness, profitability
Methods of measuring size: employees, output, capital employed
Concept of diseconomies, examples: communication, commitment, coordination
Benefits to country/economy: jobs, exports, choice, investment
Drawbacks to country/economy: local sales reduction, profit repatriation

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'exchange rate'?
What is meant by 'capital employed'?
Identify and explain two ways NBV's managers could use its financial accounts to help make decisions.
Identify and explain two diseconomies of scale that NBV might experience.
Do you think NBV's decision to set up a factory will only bring drawbacks to other businesses in country B? Justify your answer.
